The Motorola Moto G50 was released in 2021. It has no device package yet. A console-only Nura edge root filesystem (OpenRC) boots on the vendor 5.4 kernel and answers over ssh, and Debian 13 runs fully on the same kernel with WiFi and Bluetooth. The notes below are meant as groundwork for a proper port.

The tested unit is an XT2137-2 owned by [[User:Gahingwoo]]. Its screen is broken, so display and touch were never tested. Everything was done over USB and WiFi.

== Contributors ==
* [[User:Gahingwoo]]

== Users owning this device ==
{{Device owners}}

== How to enter flash mode ==
Turn the phone off, then hold {{Button|Volume Down}} and {{Button|Power}} at the same time to enter fastboot.

It is also possible to enter fastboot using <code>adb</code>:
<syntaxhighlight lang="shell-session">
$ adb reboot bootloader
</syntaxhighlight>

== How to unlock the bootloader ==
Enter flash mode (see [[#How to enter flash mode]]) and follow the instructions on [https://en-us.support.motorola.com/app/standalone/bootloader/unlock-your-device-a Motorola Support]. The tested unit was already unlocked, so this was not tried on it.

== Installation ==
There is no image to install with pmbootstrap. The boot test used a boot image built from the LineageOS kernel plus a small initramfs, started with:
<syntaxhighlight lang="shell-session">
$ fastboot boot boot.img
</syntaxhighlight>
Nothing is written to the phone, and a reboot returns to whatever was installed before. The scripts, the initramfs and the way the Nura edge root was built are in [https://github.com/gahingwoo/linux-ibiza linux-ibiza].

Before flashing anything, back up <code>boot_a</code>, <code>modem*</code>, <code>modemst1</code>, <code>modemst2</code>, <code>fsg</code>, <code>fsc</code>, <code>persist</code> and the partition table.

== Notes ==
=== Android versions ===
The phone launched with Android 11. The last Motorola release is Android 12. LineageOS 24.0 (Android 17) runs on it; this was checked on the tested unit.

| Kernel source || [https://github.com/LineageOS/android_kernel_motorola_sm6375 LineageOS/android_kernel_motorola_sm6375] (GPL-2.0), Linux 5.4.302, config fragment <code>vendor/ext_config/moto-holi-ibiza.config</code>
|-
| WiFi, Bluetooth || Qualcomm WCN3990 (icnss2 with <code>wlan.ko</code>; Bluetooth over UART)
|-
| Hypervisor || The Qualcomm hypervisor owns EL2 (<code>All CPU(s) started at EL1</code>), so there is no KVM
|}

=== Things a port has to know ===
==== Kernel and boot ====
* The Android boot image is version 3 and uses the stock <code>vendor_boot</code>. The bootloader needs a legacy LZ4 ramdisk; a gzip ramdisk stacked after LZ4 does not boot.
* The kernel has no <code>CONFIG_DEVTMPFS</code>, no IPC, PID or USER namespaces, no debugfs, and no <code>CONFIG_FHANDLE</code> or autofs. The initramfs therefore mounts a tmpfs on the new root's <code>/dev</code> and fills it from <code>/sys/class/*</code> before switching root. Units that need namespaces fail unless you set <code>PrivateIPC=no</code> and similar options.
* A new systemd freezes in PID 1 with "Failed to determine whether /proc is a mount point". The likely cause is that the kernel has no <code>name_to_handle_at</code> (no <code>CONFIG_FHANDLE</code>) and its <code>statx</code> returns no mount id (added in Linux 5.8). Debian's systemd 257 boots on the same kernel, and Nura edge boots with OpenRC.

==== WiFi ====
* The WiFi firmware runs in a modem protection domain, so the modem has to boot. The downstream kernel drops userspace QRTR registrations made after the modem link comes up, so <code>qrtr</code>, <code>pd-mapper</code>, <code>tqftpserv</code> and <code>rmtfs</code> must already be running.
* Run <code>rmtfs</code> on copies of <code>modemst1</code>, <code>modemst2</code>, <code>fsg</code> and <code>fsc</code>, never on the real partitions: they hold the IMEI and the RF calibration.
* <code>cnss-daemon</code> and <code>pm-service</code> are Android (bionic) binaries. They run from the read-only <code>system</code> and <code>vendor</code> partitions in a chroot, with a small <code>LD_PRELOAD</code> that fakes the property service and the SELinux calls. The board data file <code>bdwlan_ibiza_ipa.bin</code> must be visible at <code>/vendor/firmware_mnt/image</code>.
* <code>wlan.ko</code> is built with <code>PANIC_ON_BUG</code>. Never <code>rmmod wlan</code> after a failed load.

==== Bluetooth ====
* The host UART runtime-suspends when idle, and closing the tty drops RTS so the chip goes to sleep. Keep the tty open from a resident process and <code>btattach</code> to a pty.
* The kernel's <code>hci_qca</code> sends a 243-byte first TLV segment that kills the chip's parser; a 16-byte first segment works. Load the firmware from userspace.

==== Partitions and slots ====
* '''Never resize or add entries to the GPT of the UFS LUN that holds <code>super</code> and <code>userdata</code>, and do not use sgdisk on it.''' Afterwards the bootloader reads nothing on that LUN: <code>cid</code> and <code>imei</code> come back empty and <code>fastboot boot</code> fails with "No Media". To recover, run <code>fastboot flash partition gpt.bin</code> with the file from the stock firmware package.
* With no Android to call <code>markBootSuccessful</code>, the slot's retry counter drops on every boot. Either set the successful bit (bit 54 of the <code>boot_a</code> GPT attributes, rewriting both tables and their CRCs) or reset the counter with <code>fastboot set_active a</code>. <code>fastboot flash boot_a</code> resets the attributes.
